title: Biodiversity

source.name: Wikipedia — Biodiversity
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Biodiversity is the variability of life on Earth. It can be measured on various levels, for example, genetic variability, species diversity, ecosystem diversity, and phylogenetic diversity. Diversity is not distributed evenly on Earth — it is greater in the tropics as a result of the warm climate and high primary productivity in the region near the equator. Tropical forest ecosystems cover less than one-fifth of Earth's terrestrial area and contain about 50% of the world's species. There are latitudinal gradients in species diversity for both marine and terrestrial taxa.

Since life began on Earth, six major mass extinctions and several minor events have led to large and sudden drops in biodiversity. The Phanerozoic aeon (the last 540 million years) marked a rapid growth in biodiversity via the Cambrian explosion. In this period, the majority of multicellular phyla first appeared. The next 400 million years included repeated, massive biodiversity losses. Those events have been classified as mass extinction events. In the Carboniferous, rainforest collapse may have led to a great loss of plant and animal life. The Permian–Triassic extinction event, 251 million years ago, was the worst; vertebrate recovery took 30 million years.

Human activities have led to an ongoing biodiversity loss and an accompanying loss of genetic diversity. This process is often referred to as Holocene extinction, or the sixth mass extinction. For example, it was estimated in 2007 that up to 30% of all species will be extinct by 2050. Destroying habitats for farming is a key reason why biodiversity is decreasing today. Climate change also plays a role. This can be seen for example in the effects of climate change on biomes. This anthropogenic extinction may have started toward the end of the Pleistocene, as some studies suggest that the megafaunal extinction event that took place around the end of the last ice age partly resulted from overhunting.

Biodiversity is most commonly used to replace the more clearly-defined and long-established terms, species diversity and species richness. However, there is no concrete definition for biodiversity, as its definition continues to be reimagined and redefined. To give a couple of examples, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) defined biodiversity in 2019 as "the variability that exists among living organisms (both within and between species) and the ecosystems of which they are part." The World Health Organization updated its website's definition of biodiversity to be the "variability among living organisms from all sources." Both these definitions, although broad, give a current understanding of what is meant by the term biodiversity.

questions.q: What does the first paragraph suggest about climate and biodiversity?
options: A warm climate near the equator goes together with a richer variety of life
Tropical forests cover more than half of the land area of the planet
Variety of life is spread evenly across all parts of the Earth
Most of the world’s species are found in the coldest parts of the planet
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: đa dạng sinh học lớn hơn ở vùng nhiệt đới do khí hậu ấm và năng suất sơ cấp cao gần xích đạo; không phân bố đều.

questions.q: What is remarkable about tropical forests, according to paragraph 1?
options: They take up a small part of the land but hold a very large share of species
They contain mainly species that are also found in cooler regions
They take up most of the land but hold only a modest number of species
They hold fewer species than the oceans, even though they are very large
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: rừng nhiệt đới chiếm “less than one-fifth” diện tích đất liền nhưng chứa “about 50%” số loài.

questions.q: What does the writer imply about the Permian–Triassic extinction event?
options: It was the first of the six major mass extinctions in the history of life
It happened soon after the Cambrian explosion and ended the growth in species
It was caused by the collapse of the rainforests of the Carboniferous
It was the worst of all, and vertebrates took exceptionally long to recover
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: “was the worst; vertebrate recovery took 30 million years”. Sự sụp đổ rừng mưa thuộc kỉ Carbon, không phải nguyên nhân được nêu cho Permi–Trias.

questions.q: Which cause of today’s biodiversity loss does the text emphasise most?
options: Hunting large animals for sport in the modern age
Overfishing in the tropical seas that lie near the equator
Clearing natural habitats in order to create farmland
The spread of large cities across deserts and mountains
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “Destroying habitats for farming is a key reason why biodiversity is decreasing today.” Biến đổi khí hậu chỉ được nêu thêm là “also plays a role”.

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about the beginnings of human-caused extinction?
options: It is certain that early farming caused the first extinctions in history
It started with the Industrial Revolution and the use of powerful machines
It may be far older than industry, perhaps linked to overhunting in the ice age
It began only in 2007, when scientists first managed to measure species loss
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: tuyệt chủng do con người “may have started toward the end of the Pleistocene”; một số nghiên cứu cho rằng việc săn bắn quá mức “partly resulted” – cách diễn đạt dè dặt (may, some studies suggest).

questions.q: What point does the writer make about the definition of biodiversity?
options: It refers only to the number of different species living in one place
The United Nations and the World Health Organization use exactly the same wording
It is a precise, long-established term that is now being replaced by “species richness”
No single agreed definition exists; organisations describe it broadly but differently
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “there is no concrete definition”; FAO và WHO đưa ra hai định nghĩa khác nhau về câu chữ nhưng đều rộng. Thuật ngữ này thay thế “species diversity/richness”, không phải ngược lại.

questions.q: Biodiversity can be measured at more than one level, for example genes and ecosystems.
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: đo ở nhiều cấp độ – genetic variability, species diversity, ecosystem diversity…

questions.q: The Cambrian explosion produced more species than any later period in the history of life.
questions.explain: Đoạn 2 chỉ nói đó là giai đoạn tăng trưởng nhanh khi phần lớn các ngành đa bào xuất hiện; không so sánh số loài với các giai đoạn sau.

Diversity is not distributed evenly on Earth

vocab.def: the death of all members of a species
the natural home of a plant or animal

vocab.def: clear and definite; real rather than general
vocab.ex: there is no concrete definition for biodiversity

coll.vi: sự suy giảm đa dạng sinh học

coll.ex: an accompanying loss of genetic diversity

str.s: is not distributed evenly … — it is greater in …
str.vi: không phân bố đều … — nó lớn hơn ở …
str.ex: Diversity is not distributed evenly on Earth — it is greater in the tropics as a result of the warm climate and high primary productivity in the region near the equator.
str.explain: Dấu gạch ngang nối một nhận xét giải thích; as a result of + danh từ nêu nguyên nhân.

str.ex: rainforest collapse may have led to a great loss of plant and animal life
str.explain: may have + V3: suy đoán về điều có thể đã xảy ra trong quá khứ.

str.ex: This process is often referred to as Holocene extinction, or the sixth mass extinction.
str.explain: Cụm bị động dùng để giới thiệu thuật ngữ khác.

str.vi: người ta ước tính năm 2007 rằng …
str.ex: it was estimated in 2007 that up to 30% of all species will be extinct by 2050
str.explain: it + bị động + that-clause: nêu một ước tính/nhận định chung.
